## Context / Problem
When a ticket's acceptance criteria stop matching reality, the completion-verification close
gate blocks the close and there is no obvious sanctioned way forward. Agents reach for
`--force-close` (which closes WITHOUT verification, leaving an uncertified ticket) or for
`--ref <old-commit>` (which verifies against the tree where the criteria still held).

**Decision (2026-07-24): both of those are the WRONG answer for stale criteria.**

Closing against criteria that no longer describe the work leaves inaccurate state in the
ticket system. The ticket permanently claims something that is not true of the codebase — and
the ticket store is the shared, durable record other agents read. A close that "passed" by
pointing at an old commit is a close whose criteria still lie.

**The correct path is: EDIT the ticket so its criteria are accurate, re-pass the plan-review
gate, then close against the corrected criteria.** The criteria end up true, the close is
genuinely verified, and the record is accurate.

This ticket is therefore a DOCUMENTATION fix, not a feature. It was originally scoped toward
building an auditable "criterion disposition" record (moot / invalidated / superseded) with
cited evidence and provenance. That is deliberately REJECTED as overbuilt for a single bug
report: it adds a whole audited sub-system to avoid an edit that authors should be making
anyway.

## Worked example (the case that prompted this)
`86a5-9221-0037-4e38`'s criteria grepped `docs/passing-code-review.md`. A later commit
(c2bfbe217) moved that guide into the package, leaving the old path a stub — so the criteria
became false. It was closed with `--ref f90850861`, the commit where the work landed, which
PASSED verification but left the ticket asserting a file check that no longer holds. Under this
decision the right move was to edit the criteria to name
`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`, re-pass plan review, and close.

## Out of scope (explicitly not building)
- An auditable criterion-disposition record (moot / invalidated-by-fix / superseded).
- An automation-owned closure path for bot-filed alert tickets.
- Any change to `--force-close`, which remains the escape hatch for a human operator's
  judgment call and correctly leaves the ticket unsigned.

## Known related gap (NOT fixed here)
Closing an epic whose plan review predates a criteria-registry change is blocked by the
plan-review close gate's `stale-regver` check, forcing a full billable re-review of an
already-executed plan. Hit twice on 2026-07-24 (86a5 and 58f2). Recorded here so it is not
lost; it needs its own ticket if it keeps costing.

## Scope
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — a short subsection under the completion close gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states that when acceptance criteria no longer match reality
      the fix is to EDIT the ticket, re-pass plan review, then close against the corrected
      criteria; verified by
      `grep -q 'criteria no longer match' docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The same passage says explicitly that closing against stale criteria — whether via
      `--force-close` or by pointing `--ref` at an older commit — leaves inaccurate state in
      the ticket system and is not the remedy; verified by
      `grep -q 'inaccurate state' docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The addition is SHORT (a single subsection, not a new document or a new mechanism).
- [ ] `make lint` and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
